newsitem.title: UK: HK STOCKS IN LONDON FIRMER, DRAGGED HIGHER BY HSBC.
newsitem.headline: HK STOCKS IN LONDON FIRMER, DRAGGED HIGHER BY HSBC.

text.p: Hong Stock stocks in London were mostly firmer on Monday, with heavyweight banking group HSBC Holdings being the star performer, dealers said.
Shares in HSBC jumped HK$5.12-1/2 to close at HK$275.12-1/2, after shares in its subsidiary Hang Seng Bank Ltd surged HK$5.50 to HK$108.50 in Hong Kong.
Hong Kong brokers said shares in Hang Seng were boosted by speculation that a Chinese third party was poised to become a shareholder in the bank. HSBC owns a 63.61 percent stake in Hang Seng Bank.
Elsewhere in London, dealers said volume was light as investors stayed on the sidelines following Friday's 156.78 point fall on Wall Street.
The Hang Seng London Reference Index gained 102.46 points to close at 16,562.93 after the Hang Seng index in Hong Kong fell 187.07 points to finish at 16,460.47.
